orientation: STINAPA requires a checkout/orientation dive for anyone new to Bonaire, regardless of certification. Book it for the morning of day 1. Shops won't release independent shore tanks until you've done it.

conditions.v: Warmest in Sep–Oct (~83°F / 28°C); averages ~81°F year-round. A 3 mm shorty or full suit; gloves are banned.
Typically 60–100+ ft on the west coast; mornings are best. Nearshore vis can drop after rain.
Rainy season is Oct–Jan, with November the wettest. Showers are usually short and often at night or early morning.
Season ends Nov 30. Bonaire lies south of the main belt and direct hits are uncommon, but tropical waves can bring west-coast chop (wind reversals).
Minimal at most leeward shore sites. Karpata, Red Slave and some Klein/south double-reef sites can run.
Allowed from 30 min after sunset at shore sites. Town Pier is guided/permit only.

bring: Your own dive computer, mask and SMB (safety sausage)
Hard-sole booties (entries are rock, rubble and concrete)
Dive flag for shore dives near boat traffic
Primary + backup torch for night dives
Rash guard / thin suit (no gloves allowed)
Cert cards + Nature Fee QR code on your phone
Log of last dive (shops ask how recently you dived)
rules: Nature Fee QR + ID: rangers check
No gloves (medical exception only), no touching or taking anything
No fish feeding, no reef hooks, no chemical light sticks
No anchoring on the reef; use moorings
Lionfish spearing only with ELF certification
Night shore diving from 30 min after sunset; Town Pier only with an operator permit
Fines cited at $25–$300; rangers do patrol
avoid: Salt Pier when a salt ship is docked: closed, no exceptions
East/windward coast unless a local shop briefs you on a wind reversal
Karpata and 1000 Steps entries in north swell; pick a house reef instead
Hilma Hooker unless you're AOW and current (60–110 ft); shore vs boat access is disputed, so ask the shop
Red Slave / southern tip as an early-week site (current)
Leaving anything in the truck at dive sites; break-ins are a long-standing problem
Expecting 2019-era coral: live coral cover fell from 24% (2019) to 9% (2025) after disease and bleaching. Fish and turtles are still great.
Last dive less than 24 h before your flight
week: Suggested: Day 1 orientation + Bari/Andrea · Day 2 1000 Steps + Oil Slick Leap · Day 3 Salt Pier (if no ship) + Angel City · Day 4 Klein boat (Forest + a shallower site) · Day 5 Karpata AM (calm only) + house-reef night · Day 6 Hilma Hooker + spare.
